title: USSR 101
description: Learn about the history of the USSR.
summary: Test your knowledge of the Soviet Union's history, leaders, and major milestones.

questions.text: Which event in 1917 led to the fall of the Russian Provisional Government and the rise of the Bolsheviks?
questions.explanationText: The October Revolution (also known as the Bolshevik Revolution), led by Vladimir Lenin, overthrew the Russian Provisional Government in 1917.

questions.text: Who was the first leader and founder of the Soviet Union (USSR)?
questions.explanationText: Vladimir Lenin was the founder of the Bolshevik party and the first head of state of the Soviet Union, established in 1922.

questions.text: What was the official name of the secret police established by the Bolsheviks in December 1917 to combat counter-revolution?
questions.explanationText: The Cheka (All-Russian Extraordinary Commission) was the first Soviet state security organization, founded by Felix Dzerzhinsky.

questions.text: Which treaty did Bolshevik Russia sign in 1918 to officially end its participation in World War I?
questions.explanationText: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed between Bolshevik Russia and the Central Powers, withdrawing Russia from WWI at the cost of significant territory.

questions.text: What economic policy did Lenin introduce in 1921, which temporarily allowed private trade and small businesses to revive the economy?
questions.explanationText: The New Economic Policy (NEP) was a more market-oriented economic policy introduced to rebuild the economy after the Russian Civil War.

questions.text: What was the name of the Red Army commander who played a key role in the Bolshevik victory during the Russian Civil War but was later exiled and assassinated?
questions.explanationText: Leon Trotsky founded the Red Army. After losing a power struggle to Stalin, he was exiled and eventually assassinated in Mexico in 1940.

questions.text: In which year was the Soviet Union (USSR) officially established?
questions.explanationText: The USSR was officially established in December 1922 by a treaty signing between the Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Transcaucasian republics.

questions.text: Which Soviet leader launched the policy of agricultural collectivization and rapid industrialization in the late 1920s?
questions.explanationText: Joseph Stalin initiated the Five-Year Plans and forced collectivization, aiming to transform the USSR from an agrarian society to an industrial superpower.

questions.text: What term is used to describe the state-run system of forced labor camps in the Soviet Union?
questions.explanationText: The Gulag was the government agency that administered the main Soviet network of forced labor camps.

questions.text: Which Soviet city was subjected to a devastating 872-day military blockade by German forces during World War II?
questions.explanationText: The Siege of Leningrad (now Saint Petersburg) lasted from 1941 to 1944, resulting in massive casualties, primarily due to starvation.

questions.text: Which battle is widely considered the major turning point of World War II on the Eastern Front?
questions.explanationText: The Battle of Stalingrad (1942–1943) ended with the surrender of the German 6th Army and turned the tide of the war in favor of the Allies.

questions.text: Who was the British Prime Minister who coined the term 'Iron Curtain' in 1946 to describe the division of Europe?
questions.explanationText: Winston Churchill delivered his famous 'Sinews of Peace' address in Fulton, Missouri, coining the phrase 'Iron Curtain'.

questions.text: Which military alliance was formed in 1955 by the Soviet Union and its Eastern European satellite states in response to West Germany joining NATO?
questions.explanationText: The Warsaw Pact was a collective defense treaty signed in Warsaw, Poland, between the USSR and seven Soviet satellite states.

questions.text: Who succeeded Joseph Stalin as the leader of the Soviet Union and initiated a period known as the 'Thaw'?
questions.explanationText: Nikita Khrushchev led the USSR during the Cold War, initiating 'De-Stalinization' and political relaxation known as the Khrushchev Thaw.

questions.text: In 1956, Khrushchev delivered a secret speech titled 'On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences.' What was its primary focus?
questions.explanationText: Delivered at the 20th Party Congress, the speech criticized Stalin's purges, the cult of personality, and gulags.

answers.text: Denouncing the crimes and excesses of Joseph Stalin
Declaring war on the United States

questions.text: What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched into space by the Soviet Union in 1957?
questions.explanationText: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, starting the Space Age and the Space Race.

questions.text: Who was the first human to travel into outer space, orbiting the Earth in April 1961?
questions.explanationText: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit of Earth in his Vostok 1 spacecraft on April 12, 1961.

questions.text: Which tense 1962 confrontation brought the US and USSR to the brink of nuclear war?
questions.explanationText: The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred when the US discovered Soviet nuclear missiles deployed in Cuba, leading to a 13-day standoff.

questions.text: Which Soviet leader succeeded Nikita Khrushchev in 1964 and led the country during a period later termed the 'Era of Stagnation'?
questions.explanationText: Leonid Brezhnev ruled from 1964 to 1982, marked by political stability but economic stagnation and military build-up.

questions.text: The invasion of which country in 1979 led to a prolonged, ten-year conflict often described as the Soviet Union's 'Vietnam War'?
questions.explanationText: The Soviet-Afghan War began in December 1979, draining Soviet military and economic resources and contributing to its collapse.

questions.text: Who became the last General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1985?
questions.explanationText: Mikhail Gorbachev introduced major reforms to revitalize the USSR but ultimately presided over its dissolution in 1991.

questions.text: What did the reform policy 'Glasnost', introduced by Mikhail Gorbachev, translate to?
questions.explanationText: Glasnost was the policy of increased transparency in government activities and freedom of information and speech.

questions.text: What did the reform policy 'Perestroika', introduced by Mikhail Gorbachev, translate to?
questions.explanationText: Perestroika referred to the restructuring of the Soviet political and economic systems, allowing some private enterprise.

questions.text: Which Soviet nuclear power plant was the site of the world's worst civilian nuclear disaster in April 1986?
questions.explanationText: The Chernobyl disaster occurred in the Ukrainian SSR, releasing massive amounts of radioactive contamination across Europe.

questions.text: What physical barrier, dividing a major European city, was opened in November 1989, symbolizing the collapse of communism in Eastern Europe?
questions.explanationText: The fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 marked the beginning of the end of the Cold War and communist regimes in Eastern Europe.

questions.text: What was the name of the attempted coup in August 1991 that sought to depose Mikhail Gorbachev and halt his reform program?
questions.explanationText: The August Coup was launched by hardline members of the Communist Party, but failed due to popular resistance led by Boris Yeltsin.

questions.text: Who was elected as the first President of the Russian Federation in June 1991, playing a key role in defeating the August Coup?
questions.explanationText: Boris Yeltsin became the leader of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic and emerged as a hero during the August Coup.

questions.text: Which agreement, signed in December 1991 by the leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus, declared the Soviet Union dissolved?
questions.explanationText: The Belavezha Accords declared that the USSR had ceased to exist and established the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

questions.text: On what date did the Soviet flag over the Kremlin fly for the last time, marking the official end of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanationText: On December 25, 1991, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the USSR, and the Soviet hammer and sickle flag was replaced by the Russian tricolor.

questions.text: How many sovereign republics emerged as independent nations following the dissolution of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanationText: The dissolution of the Soviet Union resulted in 15 independent successor states: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, and Uzbekistan.
